source.title: A Random Matrix Perspective on Mixtures of Nonlinearities in High Dimensions
source.authors: Ben Adlam; Jake Levinson; Jeffrey Pennington

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes random-feature regression and reports test-error comparisons between activation functions, but it does not test double descent over model size, training time, or sample size, nor the other listed versions. Double descent is only mentioned through cited related work.
record.gate_note: The test-error comparisons between single activations and mixtures are recorded as findings about generalization that fit none of the listed double-descent versions. Spectral-density results, training-error results, and test-error curves without separately stated numerical values are not rows for those versions. Cited results are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study derives exact asymptotic training and test errors for ridge-regularized random-feature regression, then compares activation functions and mixtures. It reports no test-error sweep over width, epochs or sample size, and no interpolation peak. Double descent appears only in cited titles ([1], [2], [10], [29]). Figure 3 varies the shape parameters φ and ψ, but only for training or memorization error. Figure 5 varies the ridge γ at fixed ψ and shows no peak structure. Nothing here bears on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive an exact Stieltjes-transform characterization of the random-feature spectrum. From it they obtain training error for noisy autoencoding and test error under a linear teacher. They show some activation mixtures provably beat the best single nonlinearity.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes ridge-regularized random-feature regression; it does not apply the double-descent size, epoch, or sample-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error depends on the activation choice, mixture settings, and regularization setting in the reported comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: In linear-teacher random-feature regression (φ=1/2, ψ=1/8, σε²=2, γ=0.2), a Bernoulli mixture of activations gets test error ≈0.783, versus ≈0.945 for the best single nonlinearity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixtures of activation functions can lower random-feature regression test error below that of the best single activation when the ridge is suboptimal.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The reported numerical comparisons concern activation-function choices rather than the double-descent axes or peak; the empirical mixture estimate is reported over 10 trials.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the listed versions: the study does not report results testing them. Other test-error curves are presented graphically without separate numerical values.

untested.parts: Model-size sweep of test error and a peak at the interpolation threshold. ψ is fixed in the test-error results.
Test error over training time. Only closed-form ridge solutions are studied.
Effect of sample size near the threshold on test error.
Second descent past interpolation for any model class.
Prediction of peak location by an effective-complexity measure.
Role of label noise or variance in a peak, multiple peaks, and removal of a peak by optimal regularization. Fig. 5 shows test error vs γ at fixed size only.
Recounting effective parameters to turn the second descent into a U-shaped curve.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (cites_only), tranche (T6) and row links are confirmed. The training-error curves over φ and ψ (Fig. 3) concern memorization, not test error, so they do not bear on V1 or V3.

versions.untested_parts: The model-size test-error fall-rise-fall shape and its peak near the training-set interpolation threshold.
The test-error shape over training epochs.
Whether increasing sample size near the interpolation threshold raises test error.
Whether risk falls again as capacity grows past interpolation across model classes.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
The roles of label noise or variance in the peak; multiple peaks; and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
Whether appropriate effective parameter counting turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: random feature regression with a single activation function
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test error for a linear-teacher regression task; optimized the single nonlinearity at the stated setting.
rows.note: This is a test-error comparison between activation choices, not a measurement of any listed double-descent version.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. It is the best single-activation test error (≈0.945 at ζ≈0.634) at fixed φ=1/2, ψ=1/8, γ=0.2. That is an activation-choice comparison, not a double-descent measure. It serves as the baseline for r2.

rows.subject: random feature regression with a Bernoulli mixture of activation functions
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test error for a linear-teacher regression task using a Bernoulli mixture of two activation functions.
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns activation mixtures, not double-descent behavior.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. It is the Bernoulli-mixture test error (≈0.783 theory; 0.785 ±0.035 simulated) compared with the best single activation. It bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
